pins.title: What to Say First When Your Teen Fails a Test
pins.description: A failed test can trigger a lecture before either of you knows what actually happened. Start with: “That hurts. This result is one event—not your identity.” Let the score land, then return to the marked work later. Save this script for the next hard result. #ParentingTeens #StudySkills #ParentScripts

pins.title: A Three-Step Reset After Your Teen Fails a Test
pins.description: After a poor test result, use FEEL → FACTS → ONE CHANGE. First name the disappointment. Later, inspect where the marks went. Then let your teen choose one method to test before the next assessment. Save this three-step reset for a calmer, more useful conversation. #ParentingTeens #SchoolStress #StudyTips

pins.title: Don’t Ask This Question at the Door After a Test
pins.description: “Did you even study?” turns the first minute into an investigation. Try: “You look disappointed. We’ll talk about the details later.” Give the result time to land, then examine the marked work when everyone is steadier. Save this line for the walk in from school. #ParentingTeens #ParentScripts #SchoolStress
pins.alt_text: A discouraged teenage boy reads a test in the entryway while his mother waits calmly; the Pin advises delaying detailed questions.
pins.provider_card_text: Scheduled for Mon, 28/9 08:30 am Don’t Ask This Question at the Door After a Test Parenting Teens

pins.title: Inspect the Marked Work, Not Your Teen’s Character
pins.description: A poor score is not a character report. Ask where the marks went: knowledge, question wording, time, checking, or a repeated error. Keep “I studied” concrete without cross-examining, and find the smallest useful fact before choosing a change. Save this checklist. #ParentingTeens #StudySkills #Learning
pins.alt_text: An overhead parent checklist asks where marks were lost and what preparation happened beside a marked maths paper.
pins.provider_card_text: Scheduled for Tue, 29/9 07:30 pm Inspect the Marked Work, Not Your Teen’s Character Parenting Teens

pins.title: One Study Change Your Teen Can Choose and Test
pins.description: Do not replace one failed test with a whole new life plan. Match one change to the evidence: recall questions for a knowledge gap, timed practice for a time problem, or teacher feedback when the marking is unclear. Let your teen choose, then review whether the method was usable. #ParentingTeens #StudyTips #TeenIndependence
